newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Cypriots say may take Varosha in missile row.
newsitem.headline: Turk Cypriots say may take Varosha in missile row.

text.p: Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash said on Friday he would integrate a disputed no-man's-land into the Turkish sector of the island if Cyprus did not drop plans to buy Russian anti-aircraft missiles.

"If the S-300 missile systems that the Greek Cypriots are determined to buy despite all serious warnings are imported to Cyprus then we will go towards socially and economically incorporating the (Varosha) region into (Famagusta)," Denktash said in a statement distributed by the Turkish foreign ministry.
Varosha is a Turkish-held resort that has been closed off since the island was divided in 1974. Most of the property in the resort is owned by Greek Cypriots.

"We will take all measures we see as necessary as long as the decision to buy the S-300 missile systems and as long as the Greek Cypriots insist on continuing with the behaviour that is deepening the confidence crisis on the island," Denktash said.

Cyprus has declared its intention to buy the Russian surface-to-air missiles to prevent possible Turkish air strikes. The missiles could neutralise Turkish air superiority on the island. Turkey has threatened to strike at the missile launch pads if the S-300s are deployed.

There are 30,000 Turkish troops in the northern third of Cyprus while the internationally recognised Cyprus government controls the Greek Cypriot south. The island has been divided since 1974, when Turkish troops invaded in response to a coup engineered by the military junta then ruling Greece.
